problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 18 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above.
Find the unknown functions $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ in the general solution to the system, shown below.

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}f(t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}g(t) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}]
$$

*Hint: One of the eigenvalues of the matrix is ${\lambda }_{1}=12\text{i}.$*

worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 18 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

We are given that the eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=12\text{i}.$ 

Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors. For ${\lambda }_{1}=12\text{i},$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}-12\text{i} & 18 \\ -8 & -12\text{i}\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3\text{i} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}$ is 
${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=12\text{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{\text{12i}t}.
$$

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{\text{12i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t)) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t)+2\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t)-3\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t)+2\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${w}_{1}$ and ${w}_{2}$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t) \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
f(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(12t),\,g(t)=-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(12t).
$$
